Why Authentic Afghan Chicken Soup Hits Differently Than Canned Broth

When chilly evening winds blow across the San Fernando Valley or winter rains roll in off the Santa Monica mountains, generic canned soups and watered-down commercial broths simply don't satisfy. Traditional Afghan chicken soup—known as Shorba-e Murgh—is an ancient Silk Road healing recipe crafted for deep restoration and genuine warmth.

At Bigi Awasaana, we start every batch by gently simmering bone-in Zabiha Halal chicken over low heat for hours. As the chicken gently braises, it releases collagen, bioavailable minerals, and natural gelatin into a rich golden broth. We infuse this simmering base with cracked coriander seed, ground cumin, golden turmeric, crushed black pepper, fresh ginger, and slow-melted yellow split peas that lend a velvety, satisfying body without adding heavy cream, artificial starches, or flour.

Yes. All chicken, beef, and lamb used at Bigi Awasaana is strictly 100% hand-slaughtered Zabiha Halal. Our soup broth contains zero artificial bouillons, pork gelatin, or generic machine-cut poultry.

Does the soup contain dairy or gluten?

Our Afghan chicken soup is naturally dairy-free and simmered without flour thickeners. It is thickened naturally with slow-simmered yellow split peas and tender pulled chicken.

How is the soup packaged for takeout?

We package our chicken soup in heavy-duty, leak-resistant insulated bowls designed to keep the broth steaming hot during your drive across Reseda, Tarzana, Encino, or Woodland Hills.
